covers.quote: Use images for links only if they meet a user need.

rules.quote: Use text for links in most cases.
rules.specification: Links should generally consist of anchor text rather than linked images, unless an image meets a specific user need.
rules.violation_condition: a link implemented using an image rather than anchor text, without meeting a specific user need
when: Unless an image link meets a specific user need.
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Core instruction on using text rather than images for links.

rules.quote: If you do use images, accurately describe the link with alt text. Don’t describe the image itself.
rules.violation_condition: an image link whose alt text describes the visual appearance of the image rather than the link destination/purpose, or lacks alt text
when: When using an image as a hyperlink.
rules.why: G-2: Specific rule for image links requiring alt text to describe the link rather than the image.

rules.quote: Link directly to the specific page that the user needs to go to, not the homepage.
rules.violation_condition: a link pointing to a website's homepage instead of the specific relevant target page (deep linking)
rules.why: G-2: Deep linking instruction.

covers.quote: Include document title, file type and size when linking to files
Give users the information they need to decide whether to download the file by providing the:
document title (not the file name)
the file type
the file size in kilobytes (kB) or megabytes (MB).

examples.note: Link text includes document title, file type, and file size.

parts.quote: You can read more about our financial position in the
Digital Transformation Agency Annual Report 2019–20
[PDF 1.98 MB]

rules.quote: Include all this information in the link text
rules.violation_condition: a link to a non-HTML file that omits the document title, file type, or file size in kB or MB from the link text, or uses the file name instead of the document title
when: When linking to non-HTML documents and files.
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Consolidated candidate heading and list into the actionable instruction.

covers.quote: Write link text that makes the destination clear
Links like ‘click here’ or ‘more information’ don’t give the user any information about the destination.
Write link text that makes the destination and purpose of the link clear.

examples.note: Descriptive link destination.

parts.quote: Find out more about our upcoming events on our Eventbrite page.

examples.note: Generic link text 'Click here'.

parts.quote: Click here to find out about our upcoming meetups.

rules.quote: Write link text that describes the destination in clear language.
rules.violation_condition: link text that does not describe its destination out of context, such as 'click here' or 'more information'
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Core rule on descriptive link anchor text.

covers.quote: Don’t use exit modals

rules.quote: Don’t use these to tell users they are leaving your site when they use external links.
rules.violation_condition: an exit modal or exit pop-up alert alerting users that they are navigating to an external website
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Prohibition against exit modals on external links.

covers.quote: Include keywords at the start of links
Using relevant words at the start of links is called ‘frontloading’.
Only link the keywords.

examples.note: Keywords placed earlier.

parts.quote: Attend next month’s Brisbane workshop for developers and writers.

examples.note: Keywords not frontloaded.

parts.quote: Attend a Brisbane workshop for developers and writers next month.

rules.quote: Keep them concise and put the most important words at the start of the link.
rules.specification: The key topic words should be placed at the start of the anchor text.
rules.violation_condition: link text that fails to frontload the most important keywords at the beginning of the link
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Rule on frontloading keywords in links.

covers.quote: Put most links at the end of sentences

examples.note: Link is placed at the end of the sentence.

parts.quote: Find out your eligibility for a payment by filling out the application form.

examples.note: Link is placed early in the sentence.

parts.quote: You need to fill out the application form to find out if you are eligible for a payment.

rules.quote: If it’s important for users to understand all your content, put links at the end of sentences.
rules.specification: Links should be placed at the end of sentences rather than at the beginning or middle to avoid distracting users before reading the full sentence.
rules.violation_condition: a link embedded at the start or middle of a sentence when reading the full sentence is important for user comprehension
when: When it is important for users to understand all content in the sentence.
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Sentence position of links.

covers.quote: Write short calls to action that explain what they do

examples.note: Concise call to action describing what happens next.

parts.quote: Start your application

examples.note: Vague 'Click here' call to action.

parts.quote: Click here to apply

rules.quote: Use concise keywords for call-to-action text or buttons. Accurately describe what will happen next.
rules.violation_condition: call-to-action or button text using vague phrases like 'Click here to apply' instead of concise, descriptive action keywords
when: When writing text for calls to action or buttons.
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Rule governing call-to-action link/button text.

covers.quote: Link email addresses not names
Use the mailto: prefix in the URL but not in the link text.

examples.note: Email address used as anchor text.

parts.quote: belinda.bloggs@dta.gov.au

examples.note: Person's name used as anchor text for an email link.

parts.quote: Belinda Bloggs

rules.quote: To link to an email address, use the email address as the link text so it’s not mistaken for a website address.
rules.violation_condition: a link to an email address that uses a person's name or other text instead of the email address itself as the visible link text, or includes 'mailto:' in the visible text
when: When linking to an email address.
rules.why: G-1, G-2, G-4: Specific rule regarding linking email addresses.

covers.quote: Open links in the same browser tab or window
In all cases, give users contextual information in the link to explain why a link will open in a new window or tab.

rules.quote: Set links to open in the same browser window or tab by default.
rules.violation_condition: a link configured to open in a new tab or window without contextual explanation or a specific task-based need
when: Unless opening in a new tab/window is necessary (such as logging on to a secure website, filling out a multi-step form, or downloading a document) and contextual information is provided explaining why.
rules.why: G-1, G-2, G-4: Default link target window behavior and exceptions.

covers.quote: Use the same homepage links across the site

rules.quote: You must include a homepage link in your main navigation.
rules.violation_condition: a main navigation menu that lacks a homepage link
rules.why: G-1, G-4: Mandatory navigation requirement.

rules.quote: Add homepage links to the agency name or site title and the Commonwealth Coat of Arms image. Place these links in the top left part of the page.
rules.violation_condition: agency name/site title or Commonwealth Coat of Arms image not linked to the homepage, or not placed in the top left part of the page
rules.why: G-2, G-4: Specific header homepage link requirement.
